A.explanation: Momentum is a vector because $p = mv$ and velocity has direction, so momentum has both magnitude and direction.

B.explanation: Speed is a scalar because it is the magnitude of velocity and has no direction.

C.explanation: Temperature is a scalar because it is described fully by a magnitude in $\text{K}$ or $^{\circ}\text{C}$ with no direction.

D.explanation: Young modulus is a scalar because it is a ratio of stress to strain with a value in $\text{Pa}$ and no direction.

hints: Compare momentum with speed in the list - one includes the direction of motion and the other is only how fast.
Recall the defining equation $p = mv$ and ask whether the velocity $v$ in it needs a direction.
Check temperature and Young modulus - both are fully stated by a number and unit with no direction to assign.
walkthrough: Recall the test for this question: a vector has both magnitude and direction, while a scalar has magnitude only.
Use the defining relation for momentum: $p = mv$, where $m$ is scalar mass and $v$ is velocity.
Since velocity is a vector with direction, multiplying by mass gives momentum the same direction, so momentum is a vector.
Check the others: speed is the magnitude of velocity only, temperature is specified by value alone, and Young modulus is a material constant specified by value alone.
Therefore only momentum meets the vector test. This is option A.
